content.1_identity_non_merger_with_namesakes:
- **Person**: David J. McComas, Ph.D. (Princeton faculty page name spelling: "David J. McComas"; Wikipedia: "David John McComas"; born May 22, 1958, per Wikipedia).
- **Current title (per Princeton Department page)**: Professor of Astrophysical Sciences, Princeton University; Participating Faculty in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering. Formerly Princeton University Vice President for the Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory (PPPL) from 2016 to September 2, 2024. Source: Princeton Department of Astrophysical Sciences faculty page, https://web.astro.princeton.edu/people/david-j-mccomas ; Space Physics at Princeton group page, https://spacephysics.princeton.edu/people/david-j-mccomas-phd ; Princeton news, Aug. 28, 2024, https://www.princeton.edu/news/2024/08/28/mccomas-concludes-service-vice-president-pppl-nasa-mission-nears-launch ; Wikipedia biographical entry, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_J._McComas .
- **Group**: Founder of the Space Physics at Princeton group, https://spacephysics.princeton.edu/people/david-j-mccomas-phd .
- **Research topics match**: Heliospheric physics, solar wind, interstellar boundary, instrumentation — confirmed by NASA IMAP mission profile and Princeton group mission text (https://web.astro.princeton.edu/people/david-j-mccomas ; https://science.nasa.gov/mission/imap ; https://imap.princeton.edu/ ).
- **Email**: dmccomas@princeton.edu (consistent with Princeton's standard faculty email convention; was not directly tested in this research because the inbox is unreachable from the sandbox).
- **Namesake disambiguation (explicit)**: The LinkedIn public profile at https://www.linkedin.com/in/david-mccomas-29571921 is for "David McComas — President European Equities Corporation," based in Clearwater, FL (https://realtyzapp.com/Profiles/EuroEquities ; https://rocketreach.co/david-mccomas-email_27972231). He is NOT the Princeton astrophysicist; he is a commercial real estate executive and is excluded from this lead. This is recorded here to forestall any future merger.
content.2_recent_active_funding_announced_on_or_:
- **NASA Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe (IMAP) — PI leadership and Princeton-side involvement**
  - **Funder**: NASA (Heliophysics program); spacecraft built by Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL).
  - **Title of work**: "Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe (IMAP)" — NASA's heliophysics mission to map the boundary of the heliosphere and study the interstellar medium / solar wind interaction.
  - **Public amount + currency**: No public Princeton share or total prime cost was located in official NASA or Princeton public pages. NASA line-item mission cost is not present in any of the extracted Princeton, NASA mission, or APL pages. (The Planetary Society reported FY2026 NASA budget at ~$24.44 B but did not disaggregate IMAP; https://planetary.org/articles/advocacy-success-fy2026-nasa-budget .)
  - **Award / announcement context**: Selected by NASA in June 2018 per Daily Princetonian, https://www.dailyprincetonian.com/article/2025/09/princeton-news-broadfocus-nasa-princeton-imap-launch-spacex-mission-david-mccomas ; originally targeted for 2024 launch (https://www.scienceaq.com/Article/Astronomy/63338.html ); launch re-targeted Sept 2025 per Princeton IMAP news (https://imap.princeton.edu/news/nasa-targets-september-2025-launch-heliophysics-missions ); reached L1 Jan 12, 2026 (https://www.jhuapl.edu/news/news-releases/260112-imap-arrives-l1 ).
  - **Project dates**: Mission activity spans 2018 (selection) through the operational L1 phase (started Jan 2026); IMAP Princeton timeline page lists 2018-2026 milestones (https://imap.princeton.edu/ ).
  - **Status**: Active as of latest operational milestone — orbit insertion at L1 in January 2026.
  - **Person's role**: Principal Investigator (PI) (https://www.scienceaq.com/Article/Astronomy/63338.html ; https://imap.princeton.edu/ ; https://www.jhuapl.edu/destinations/missions/imap ).
  - **Direct source URLs**:
    - Princeton University IMAP mission hub: https://imap.princeton.edu/
    - NASA mission page: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/imap
    - APL mission page: https://www.jhuapl.edu/destinations/missions/imap
    - Princeton news (post-launch): https://www.princeton.edu/news/2026/03/04/imap-opens-new-era-heliosphere-science-and-space-weather
    - Princeton news (Sept 2025 launch feature): https://www.princeton.edu/news/2025/09/21/meet-imap-leaders-dave-mccomas-and-jamie-rankin
  - **Classification important**: This is **mission/program funding** administered by NASA and built by APL. It is **not** a competitive research grant in the usual NSF/NIH/Helios-DRIVE/ROSES sense. The query specification asked to distinguish them, so IMAP is reported here as "Mission Budget + PI appointment" rather than as a discrete competitive grant.

- **Other competitive-grant records checked**:
  - **NSF Award Search** for the literal phrase "McComas" AND "Princeton" with the "Active Awards" filter returned 0 records (URL: https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/simpleSearchResult?queryText=%22McComas%22+%22Princeton%22&ActiveAwards=true ). An earlier suggested NSF record AWD_ID 2441665 ("CAREER: Unsupervised and Autonomous Reinforcement Learning of Skills," dated July 9, 2025) was checked; that award is in the IIS (Information & Intelligent Systems) division and its Princeton recipient is unrelated to heliophysics — it is **not** David McComas and **not** McComas-led funding (https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/show-award?AWD_ID=2441665 ).
  - **Department of Energy (PPPL line)**: McComas stepped down as Princeton VP for PPPL on Sept 2, 2024; PPPL is a U.S. DOE national lab managed by Princeton — his leadership ended, so any PPPL-line DOE funding flowing through his VP role is no longer attributed to him (https://www.princeton.edu/news/2024/08/28/mccomas-concludes-service-vice-president-pppl-nasa-mission-nears-launch ).
  - **No other competitive grant announcement** for David McComas at Princeton dated on or after 2024-01-01 with public amount and award metadata was located on official funder databases: **No verified public evidence found** beyond IMAP on the open-web pages reachable from this research.

content.4_linkedin_evidence:
- **Public LinkedIn profile for David J. McComas the astrophysicist**: Not directly indexed in available search results. Searches against `linkedin.com "David McComas" Princeton` etc. produced only the namesake in real estate (https://www.linkedin.com/in/david-mccomas-29571921 ), Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory's company page (https://www.linkedin.com/company/princeton-plasma-physics-lab ), and unrelated individuals. **No verified public LinkedIn profile URL** for the astrophysicist was recovered.
- **Public LinkedIn posts about McComas's group hiring**: None specifically about the Space Physics at Princeton postdoc / senior research posting were recovered in the searches conducted. (A Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory company page exists at https://www.linkedin.com/company/princeton-plasma-physics-lab but does not list it as a profile of the astrophysicist.)
- **Misattribution trap recorded**: The Princeton news article on his PPPL departure includes a "Share on LinkedIn" link (https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?url=https://www.princeton.edu/news/2024/08/28/mccomas-concludes-service-vice-president-pppl-nasa-mission-nears-launch ), but this is the standard share button — **not** a LinkedIn post by McComas himself.
- **Namesake cleanup**: The leading David McComas on LinkedIn is the European Equities Corporation president (Clearwater, FL). Identity verification has been performed; this profile is excluded.
content.5_confidence_and_caveats:
- **Identity**: HIGH confidence. Four independent Princeton-affiliated pages plus Wikipedia corroborate name, title, group, citation record, and prior VP-for-PPPL role; Wikipedia page notes birth date May 22, 1958 and alma mater MIT (B.S.), UCLA (M.S., Ph.D.). Email `dmccomas@princeton.edu` was not confirmed by direct mail delivery (out of scope of available tools); the format is consistent with Princeton's standard faculty naming, and the same email is referenced on the Space Physics at Princeton group page (https://spacephysics.princeton.edu/people/david-j-mccomas-phd ).
- **Funding**: IMAP PI leadership is HIGH confidence. Note that this is **mission funding**, not a "grant" in the conventional NSF/NIH ROSES competitive sense; the task explicitly asked to distinguish them, so I have flagged it. The total prime contract cost was not located on any public NASA/APL/Princeton page I extracted — **No verified public evidence found** for IMAP mission cost as a single number.
- **Other 2024+ competitive grants**: NSF Award Search returned zero active awards; no other funder database was reachable in this sandbox beyond NSF and open-web news. **No verified public evidence found** for any additional competitive grant since 2024-01-01 to McComas as PI at Princeton.
- **Open positions**: The Space Physics Group job posting is public on the lab and HERC; missing fields (deadline, posted date, salary, contact) are not on the public pages visited — applicants need to follow the application route on the official URL. The departmental AAS posting was a Closed/Historical record included because it appeared in the 2026-01-01+ window.
- **LinkedIn**: Search coverage was sufficient to confirm the leading David McComas on LinkedIn is a real-estate namesake. **No verified public LinkedIn profile URL** for the astrophysicist was located.
- **Mission budget vs grant caveat**: If downstream tooling downstream requires a strict "(competitive) grant" answer distinct from "PI-led mission," IMAP should be tagged as a NASA PI mission, not a grant; alternative terminology is "Funder-program funding directed through NASA HQ's heliophysics mission line."
